text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chief Justice Matthew Ngulube on Monday declared president Frederick Chiluba and four opposition candidates successful nominees for the republican presidency.

- Police have arrested a Lusaka resident said to have forcibly collected voters cards from intending voters. The opposition United National Independence Party (UNIP) denied reports that it had been buying cards from the electorate.
- Hundreds of aspiring parliamentary candidates from the ruling party and the opposition peacefully lodged their nominations on Monday, ahead of elections on November 18.

- The Zimbabwe High Commission on Monday dismissed as unfounded, comparisons between the boycott of general elections by some Zambian oppposition parties and Zimbabwe's electoral experience. High Commissioner Tirivafi Kangai said Zimbabwe's opposition did not boycott the elections as reported.
